chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn and others narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq al-Ash‘arī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Aṭiyyah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
Recite by the grave of ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn whatever you wish.

key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn, also known as Imam al-Sajjad (a.s.)

ai.seo_question: What should be recited at the grave of Imam Sajjad (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the flexibility (tawassu') in the specific wording of supplications during the ziyarah of Imam al-Baqir (a.s.), emphasizing that the sincerity of the visitor matters more than rigid formulaic recitation. Historically, this reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of valuing both prescribed liturgies and personal devotion, allowing the visitor to express their love and needs in their own words. It underscores the accessibility of the Imams' graves as places of direct spiritual connection.
